regulatory.name: Medical Devices Regulations 2002 (as amended)
regulatory.summary: UK statutory framework governing classification, conformity assessment, and MHRA registration of medical devices placed on the UK market.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — Sentinel's fall-detection and emergency-call pathway creates a credible argument for medical device classification; report proposes Class I 'mobility aid with safety features' at launch with an upgrade path to Class IIa once the emergency-call pathway is validated. MHRA classification decision must be obtained before first shipment.
regulatory.designImpact: Class I requires a Declaration of Conformity and MHRA registration before UK market placement; technical file must document intended purpose, risk management, and clinical evaluation. If reclassified to Class IIa, a UK Approved Body must audit the QMS and technical file, adding 6–18 months to the programme.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: MHRA classification ruling or binding opinion; MHRA registration on the UK medical device register; Declaration of Conformity; technical file including clinical evaluation report; if Class IIa, UK Approved Body certificate.
regulatory.gapAction: Submit a formal classification query to MHRA with the intended purpose statement and the fall-detection/alarm-centre escalation pathway described; obtain written ruling before committing to Class I technical file structure.

regulatory.name: Medical devices — Application of risk management to medical devices
regulatory.summary: International standard for systematic risk management throughout the medical device lifecycle; required under UK MDR 2002 technical file.
regulatory.applicability: UK designated standard — Risk management obligation under UK MDR 2002; applies to the complete Sentinel system including fall-detection classifier, alarm escalation logic, cellular connectivity dependency, and inductive charging stand.
regulatory.designImpact: Formal hazard identification and risk control must cover: false-negative fall detection (user falls, no alert), false-positive alerts (nuisance calls to family/ARC), cellular coverage loss, battery depletion without user awareness, inductive charging failure, and handle structural failure under 100 kg gait load.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: Risk management file (hazard log, FMEA, residual risk acceptability statement) reviewed and signed by a competent person; must be maintained throughout product lifecycle.
regulatory.gapAction: Initiate risk management file using ISO 14971 process; conduct first FMEA workshop covering sensor failure modes, connectivity loss, and mechanical failure under BS EN ISO 11334-1 load cases.

regulatory.name: Medical devices — Quality management systems — Requirements for regulatory purposes
regulatory.summary: QMS standard required to support UK MDR 2002 conformity assessment, particularly if device is reclassified to Class IIa.
regulatory.applicability: UK designated standard — QMS obligation under UK MDR 2002; Class I allows self-certification but a documented QMS is expected in the technical file; Class IIa mandates UK Approved Body audit of the QMS.
regulatory.designImpact: Design controls, supplier qualification (battery, nRF9160 module, wood handle machining), post-market surveillance, and complaint handling must be documented processes from first shipment.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: ISO 13485 certificate from a UKAS-accredited certification body (if Class IIa); or documented QMS with internal audit records (if Class I self-certification route is maintained).
regulatory.gapAction: Decide QMS scope and begin gap analysis against ISO 13485 clauses; engage a regulatory consultant to draft design-control procedures before hardware design freeze.

regulatory.name: Radio Equipment Regulations 2017 (SI 2017/1206) — UK implementation of RED
regulatory.summary: UK statutory regime requiring conformity assessment, technical file, and UKCA marking for radio equipment placed on the UK market; covers LTE-M/NB-IoT cellular and GPS receiver.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — Sentinel contains an nRF9160 LTE-M/NB-IoT/GPS radio; the Radio Equipment Regulations 2017 apply to the finished product. Module-level certification (nRF9160 carries CE/UKCA) reduces but does not eliminate the system-level obligation — the integrator must confirm the module is used within its certified parameters and that the antenna installation does not invalidate module certification.
regulatory.designImpact: Antenna placement in the wood handle (RF keep-out from carbon-fibre shaft) must be documented; antenna gain and cable loss must remain within the nRF9160 module's certified RF parameters. Any custom antenna design triggers additional RF testing. Inductive charging stand also falls under RED if it contains a radio (check Qi implementation).
regulatory.evidenceRequired: UKCA Declaration of Conformity for the finished Sentinel product referencing Radio Equipment Regulations 2017; technical file including antenna integration evidence; Ofcom spectrum compliance confirmation via module certification reference; if custom antenna, UKAS-accredited RF test report.
regulatory.gapAction: Confirm nRF9160 module certification scope covers the intended antenna configuration; commission antenna placement simulation or range test in handle-mounted configuration; prepare system-level RED technical file.

regulatory.name: Electrical Equipment (Safety) Regulations 2016 (SI 2016/1101)
regulatory.summary: UK statutory low-voltage safety regime applying to electrical equipment with working voltage 50–1000 V AC or 75–1500 V DC; covers the mains-powered inductive charging stand.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — The inductive charging stand is mains-powered household electrical equipment; the Electrical Equipment (Safety) Regulations 2016 apply. The Sentinel stick itself operates at battery voltage (below LV threshold) but the stand's mains input and inductive output interface must comply.
regulatory.designImpact: Charging stand must meet IEC 60335-1 (household appliances safety) and IEC 60335-2-29 (battery chargers) as designated standards; creepage and clearance, thermal cutoff, earth continuity, and dielectric strength tests required. Inductive power transfer must not create accessible hazardous voltages.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: UKCA Declaration of Conformity for the charging stand; test report from UKAS-accredited lab demonstrating compliance with IEC 60335-1 and IEC 60335-2-29; UKCA mark on stand and packaging.
regulatory.gapAction: Engage a UKAS-accredited test house to scope IEC 60335-1/-2-29 testing for the charging stand; include dielectric strength and inductive leakage current measurements in the test plan.

regulatory.name: Electromagnetic Compatibility Regulations 2016 (SI 2016/1091)
regulatory.summary: UK statutory EMC regime requiring that apparatus does not cause harmful interference and has adequate immunity; applies to both the Sentinel stick and the charging stand.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — Both the Sentinel stick (with cellular radio, IMU, haptic actuator, and speaker) and the charging stand (inductive power transfer at switching frequency) are apparatus under the EMC Regulations 2016. The carbon-fibre shaft and wood handle create an unusual EMC enclosure that must be characterised.
regulatory.designImpact: Conducted and radiated emissions testing required for both units; immunity testing per EN 61000-4-2 (ESD, ±4 kV contact discharge on handle is specifically flagged in the report), EN 61000-4-3 (radiated immunity), EN 61000-4-6 (conducted immunity). Inductive charger switching frequency must not interfere with cellular reception during charging.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: UKCA Declaration of Conformity referencing EMC Regulations 2016; EMC test report from UKAS-accredited lab covering emissions (CISPR 32 or EN 55032) and immunity (EN 61000-4-2, -4-3, -4-6 minimum); ESD test record at ±4 kV contact on handle surfaces.
regulatory.gapAction: Include EMC test plan in hardware bring-up schedule; specify ESD protection components on all handle-accessible PCB interfaces at schematic stage; book pre-compliance EMC scan at prototype stage.

regulatory.name: UK Conformity Assessed (UKCA) Marking — Product Safety and Metrology etc. (Amendment etc.) (EU Exit) Regulations 2019 and associated statutory instruments
regulatory.summary: Umbrella UK marking scheme replacing CE marking for products placed on the Great Britain market; required across multiple statutory regimes applicable to Sentinel.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — UKCA marking is required on both the Sentinel stick and the charging stand before sale in Great Britain, covering obligations under the Radio Equipment Regulations 2017, Electrical Equipment (Safety) Regulations 2016, EMC Regulations 2016, and UK MDR 2002 (device registration). CE marking alone is no longer sufficient for GB market placement.
regulatory.designImpact: Technical files must be structured to support UKCA declarations; conformity assessment routes must use UK-recognised bodies where third-party assessment is required (e.g. Class IIa medical device). UKCA mark must appear on the product label and packaging with UK Responsible Person address.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: UKCA Declarations of Conformity for stick and stand; UK Responsible Person details on product and packaging; technical files retained for 10 years post last manufacture date.
regulatory.gapAction: Appoint a UK Responsible Person (can be the founder's UK entity); draft UKCA DoC templates for stick and stand referencing all applicable regulations; confirm label space for UKCA mark on handle underside or shaft collar.

regulatory.name: Assistive products for walking manipulated by one arm — Requirements and test methods — Part 1: Elbow crutches
regulatory.summary: Primary UK/EU standard for one-arm walking aids covering structural strength, stability, and ergonomic requirements; the governing standard for walking stick mechanical compliance.
regulatory.applicability: UK designated standard — Structural and mechanical safety of the Sentinel stick as a walking aid; demonstrates compliance with the General Product Safety Regulations 2005 (GPSR) and supports the UK MDR 2002 technical file. The report explicitly flags this standard as governing the 100 kg static and dynamic gait load case.
regulatory.designImpact: Shaft, telescoping joint, handle-to-shaft interface, and ferrule must withstand specified static load (typically 1.5× body weight = ~1500 N), fatigue cycling, and drop tests. Carbon-fibre wall thickness (1.0–1.5 mm) and telescoping collar design must be validated against these load cases. Electronics cavity must not compromise shaft cross-section below minimum structural requirement.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: Test report from accredited lab demonstrating compliance with BS EN ISO 11334-1 load and fatigue tests on the production-representative shaft assembly including the electronics cavity; structural calculation pack signed by a mechanical engineer.
regulatory.gapAction: Commission structural FEA of the upper shaft with electronics cavity at 1.0 mm and 1.5 mm wall thickness under BS EN ISO 11334-1 load cases; identify accredited test house for physical fatigue and static load testing.

regulatory.name: Secondary cells and batteries containing alkaline or other non-acid electrolytes — Safety requirements for portable sealed lithium secondary cells, and for batteries made from them, for use in portable applications — Part 2: Lithium systems
regulatory.summary: Safety standard for lithium-ion battery packs used in portable consumer and assistive products; required for the Sentinel's tubular Li-ion battery pack.
regulatory.applicability: UK designated standard — Lithium-ion battery pack within the Sentinel stick; demonstrates compliance with the Electrical Equipment (Safety) Regulations 2016 for the battery subsystem. The report specifies a PCM/BMS with over/under-charge, short-circuit, and thermal protection — these must be validated against BS EN IEC 62133-2 abuse test requirements.
regulatory.designImpact: Battery pack (cell + PCM/BMS) must pass overcharge, forced discharge, short circuit, crush, and thermal abuse tests. Custom cylindrical form factor (to fit 19–20 mm ID cavity) means off-the-shelf 18650 pack certification may not transfer — a custom pack requires its own test programme.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: BS EN IEC 62133-2 test report for the specific battery pack configuration (cell + PCM/BMS + mechanical housing) from a UKAS-accredited or IEC-recognised lab; cell supplier's UN 38.3 test summary.
regulatory.gapAction: Confirm whether 18650 cell or custom cylindrical cell will be used; obtain cell supplier's UN 38.3 certificate; scope BS EN IEC 62133-2 pack-level testing with a UKAS-accredited lab at battery pack design freeze.

regulatory.name: UN Manual of Tests and Criteria, Part III, Sub-section 38.3 — Lithium metal and lithium ion batteries
regulatory.summary: Mandatory transport safety tests for lithium cells and batteries required before road, sea, or air shipment of finished products or battery packs.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — Battery cells and packs during inbound supply chain (cell supplier to UK) and outbound distribution (finished Sentinel sticks to customers); UN 38.3 + Carriage of Dangerous Goods and Use of Transportable Pressure Equipment Regulations 2009 (CDG 2009) for road, IMDG for sea, IATA DGR for air.
regulatory.designImpact: Cells must pass altitude simulation, thermal cycling, vibration, shock, overcharge, and forced discharge tests before shipment. If a custom cylindrical cell is specified, the cell supplier must hold a valid UN 38.3 certificate for that specific cell; a change in cell chemistry or form factor invalidates existing certification.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: UN 38.3 test summary report from cell supplier for the specific cell used in production; ADR/CDG dangerous goods documentation for road transport of finished goods; IATA DGR compliance declaration for any air freight.
regulatory.gapAction: Request UN 38.3 test summary from shortlisted cell suppliers; confirm cell form factor is locked before supplier qualification to avoid re-testing; prepare CDG dangerous goods note template for outbound logistics.

regulatory.name: General Product Safety Regulations 2005 (SI 2005/1803)
regulatory.summary: UK statutory baseline safety obligation for all consumer products not covered by a more specific product safety regime; requires products to be safe and imposes post-market surveillance duties.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — Sentinel is a consumer product sold to members of the public; GPSR applies as the baseline safety net alongside and beneath the more specific regimes (MDR, RED, EES Regs). Post-market surveillance, incident reporting, and recall obligations apply from first sale.
regulatory.designImpact: Founder must establish a post-market surveillance system, maintain a complaints log, and have a documented recall procedure before first shipment. The 24/7 alarm receiving centre creates a real-time adverse event signal that must feed into the GPSR surveillance process.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: Post-market surveillance plan; complaints and incident log procedure; recall procedure document; UK Responsible Person contact details on product and in user documentation.
regulatory.gapAction: Draft post-market surveillance plan and recall procedure; establish a mechanism to capture ARC-reported incidents as product safety signals; include GPSR obligations in the regulatory affairs workplan.

regulatory.name: Product Security and Telecommunications Infrastructure Act 2022 — Part 1: Product Security
regulatory.summary: UK statutory regime requiring minimum security standards for consumer connectable products; applies to any product with network connectivity sold to UK consumers.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — Sentinel contains an LTE-M/NB-IoT cellular module with always-on connectivity and an eSIM; it is a consumer connectable product under the PSTI Act 2022. Obligations include: no default universal passwords, a published vulnerability disclosure policy, and a defined minimum security support period communicated to consumers.
regulatory.designImpact: nRF9160 firmware must not use default universal credentials; the companion app and cloud backend must have a published vulnerability disclosure policy; the founder must state the minimum period of security update support on packaging and in the app. OTA firmware update capability over LTE-M is required to deliver security patches.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: Statement of compliance with PSTI Act 2022 Schedule 1 requirements; published vulnerability disclosure policy (URL on packaging); security support period statement in user documentation; DCMS registration if required by secondary legislation.
regulatory.gapAction: Review PSTI Act 2022 Schedule 1 obligations; confirm nRF9160 firmware has no default universal password; draft vulnerability disclosure policy and publish at a stable URL; define and document the security support period before launch.

regulatory.name: Restriction of the Use of Certain Hazardous Substances in Electrical and Electronic Equipment Regulations 2012 (SI 2012/3032)
regulatory.summary: UK statutory restriction on hazardous substances (lead, mercury, cadmium, hexavalent chromium, PBBs, PBDEs, and four phthalates) in electrical and electronic equipment.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — Sentinel stick and charging stand are electrical and electronic equipment placed on the UK market; RoHS 2012 applies to all PCBs, solder, battery pack, and electronic components. Wood handle and carbon-fibre shaft are not EEE but the electronic subassemblies within them are in scope.
regulatory.designImpact: All PCBs must use lead-free solder (SAC alloy); component procurement must include RoHS declarations; battery pack chemistry must be RoHS-compliant. Supplier RoHS declarations must be collected and retained in the technical file.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: RoHS Declaration of Conformity; supplier RoHS declarations for all electronic components and PCB assemblies; material declarations (IPC-1752A or equivalent) from PCB assembly house.
regulatory.gapAction: Add RoHS compliance requirement to component procurement specification; request IPC-1752A material declarations from PCB assembly house and battery pack supplier at design freeze.

regulatory.name: Waste Electrical and Electronic Equipment Regulations 2013 (SI 2013/3113)
regulatory.summary: UK statutory producer responsibility regime requiring registration, take-back, and reporting for electrical and electronic equipment placed on the UK market.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — Sentinel stick and charging stand are EEE; the founder is a producer under WEEE Regulations 2013 and must register with an approved compliance scheme before first sale, finance collection and recycling, and mark products with the crossed-out wheelie bin symbol.
regulatory.designImpact: Product label must include WEEE symbol; user documentation must explain take-back options; battery must be designed for removal by an authorised recycler (even if not user-removable) — document the disassembly procedure for WEEE processing.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: WEEE producer registration number from an approved compliance scheme; annual WEEE return submissions; crossed-out wheelie bin mark on product and packaging; battery removal procedure in service documentation.
regulatory.gapAction: Register with a UK WEEE compliance scheme before first product sale; add WEEE symbol to label artwork; document battery removal procedure for WEEE processing in the service manual.

regulatory.code: IET Code of Practice for Electric Vehicle Charging Equipment Installation
regulatory.name: Ofcom — Wireless Telegraphy Act 2006 and Interface Requirements for LTE-M/NB-IoT devices
regulatory.summary: Ofcom spectrum licensing and interface requirements for devices using licensed cellular spectrum in the UK; LTE-M and NB-IoT operate in licensed bands requiring compliance with published interface requirements.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — nRF9160 LTE-M/NB-IoT radio operates in Ofcom-licensed spectrum; the finished product must comply with Ofcom Interface Requirements (IR 2030 or relevant IR for the bands used) and the Wireless Telegraphy Act 2006. Module-level certification covers the radio parameters but the system integrator must confirm the antenna installation does not cause out-of-band emissions.
regulatory.designImpact: Antenna placement in the wood handle must be characterised for out-of-band emissions; the dielectric collar or handle window design must not cause the antenna to radiate outside the certified module parameters. eSIM provisioning must use a UK MNO or MVNO with spectrum licences for LTE-M/NB-IoT.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: Ofcom Interface Requirement compliance confirmation via nRF9160 module certification reference; MNO/MVNO agreement confirming LTE-M/NB-IoT coverage SLA for UK; antenna integration test report confirming out-of-band emissions within module certification limits.
regulatory.gapAction: Identify target MNO/MVNO for eSIM provisioning and confirm LTE-M/NB-IoT UK coverage; obtain nRF9160 module Ofcom IR compliance documentation; include out-of-band antenna emissions check in EMC test plan.

regulatory.name: Household and similar electrical appliances — Safety — Part 1: General requirements
regulatory.summary: Designated safety standard for household electrical appliances; applies to the mains-powered inductive charging stand as a household appliance.
regulatory.applicability: UK designated standard — Inductive charging stand (mains-powered household appliance); demonstrates compliance with the Electrical Equipment (Safety) Regulations 2016. The stand is the only mains-connected element of the Sentinel system.
regulatory.designImpact: Stand must meet requirements for insulation, creepage and clearance, thermal protection, earth continuity, and dielectric strength. Inductive power transfer coil and switching electronics must not create accessible hazardous voltages. Thermal cutoff required if coil misalignment causes heating.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: Test report from UKAS-accredited lab demonstrating compliance with BS EN 60335-1 and BS EN 60335-2-29 (battery chargers); UKCA Declaration of Conformity for the stand.
regulatory.gapAction: Engage UKAS-accredited test house to scope BS EN 60335-1 and -2-29 testing for the charging stand at industrial design freeze; include thermal runaway scenario (misaligned coil, foreign object) in the test plan.

regulatory.name: Assessment of the compliance of low power electronic and electrical equipment with the basic restrictions relating to human exposure to electromagnetic fields (10 MHz–300 GHz)
regulatory.summary: Simplified SAR/EMF assessment standard for low-power radio devices held close to the body; relevant because Sentinel is a body-supported device with an always-on cellular radio.
regulatory.applicability: UK designated standard — LTE-M/NB-IoT radio in a device held in the hand and supported against the body during use; demonstrates compliance with the Radio Equipment Regulations 2017 essential requirement on human exposure to electromagnetic fields. The handle-mounted antenna placement (close to the user's hand) requires a specific SAR or EMF assessment.
regulatory.designImpact: Antenna must be positioned and oriented to keep RF exposure within ICNIRP limits for a hand-held device; antenna gain and duty cycle must be characterised in the handle-mounted configuration. If BS EN 62479 simplified assessment is insufficient (antenna too close to body), a full SAR measurement per BS EN 62209-1528 may be required.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: BS EN 62479 compliance assessment report or, if required, BS EN 62209-1528 SAR measurement report from a UKAS-accredited lab; included in the RED technical file.
regulatory.gapAction: Determine antenna separation distance from user's hand in normal use; conduct BS EN 62479 simplified assessment at prototype stage; escalate to full SAR measurement if separation distance is below the simplified-assessment threshold.

regulatory.name: Electrical Equipment (Safety) Regulations 2016 (SI 2016/1101)
regulatory.summary: UK statutory instrument implementing low-voltage directive obligations post-Brexit; requires safe design of electrical equipment operating between 50–1000 V AC or 75–1500 V DC, and underpins UKCA marking for the mains-powered variant.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — Mains-powered variant (optional AC supply input); the optional mains-powered variant places the product squarely within scope. The solar-only variant with internal LiFePO4 battery operating at low voltage may fall below the LV threshold but the mains variant does not. UKCA marking is required for UK market placement.
regulatory.designImpact: Mains input circuit must meet basic and supplementary insulation requirements, creepage and clearance distances, and fault protection. Power supply module must be designed or sourced to satisfy the Regulations; a pre-certified PSU module with UKCA/CE mark simplifies compliance but system-level integration must be re-assessed.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: Technical construction file including circuit diagrams, insulation coordination calculation, and either a test report from a UKAS-accredited lab or a declaration of conformity referencing harmonised standards (e.g. BS EN 62368-1). UKCA Declaration of Conformity and UK Responsible Person appointment.
regulatory.gapAction: Confirm whether mains variant input voltage falls within LV Regulations scope; select pre-certified PSU module; commission insulation coordination review and prepare technical file.

regulatory.name: Radio Equipment Regulations 2017 (SI 2017/1206) — UK RED
regulatory.summary: UK statutory instrument requiring radio equipment placed on the UK market to meet essential requirements for health/safety, EMC, and efficient use of spectrum; applies to Wi-Fi, cellular, and LoRa radio modules.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — Wi-Fi (2.4/5 GHz), optional LTE-M/NB-IoT cellular module, and LoRa 868 MHz ISM radio all constitute radio equipment under the Regulations. All three radio paths must be covered. Pre-certified radio modules carry their own conformity but system-level integration (antenna, enclosure, co-location) requires a fresh assessment.
regulatory.designImpact: Antenna placement, radome aperture in steel body, and inter-antenna isolation (≥λ/4 at 868 MHz ≈ 86 mm) must be validated. Co-location of Wi-Fi, cellular, and LoRa antennas requires desense and spurious emission testing at system level. Steel body requires non-metallic radome window — aperture dimensions and material must be specified and tested.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: System-level radio test report from a UKAS-accredited or Ofcom-recognised test house covering all active radio bands simultaneously; UKCA Declaration of Conformity referencing harmonised standards (BS EN 300 328 for Wi-Fi, BS EN 301 511/BS EN 301 908 for cellular, BS EN 300 220 for LoRa 868 MHz); UK Responsible Person appointment.
regulatory.gapAction: Select pre-certified Wi-Fi/BLE, cellular, and LoRa modules; engage RF test house to scope system-level co-existence and radome aperture testing; define antenna positions in ID concept model.

regulatory.name: Electromagnetic Compatibility Regulations 2016 (SI 2016/1091)
regulatory.summary: UK statutory instrument requiring electrical and electronic apparatus to neither generate electromagnetic disturbance beyond set limits nor be susceptible to such disturbance.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — Entire Hedgerow product (both solar-only and mains variants); the NPU SoC, switching power management PCBA, and solar charge controller are all potential EMC emission sources. Outdoor garden placement near other consumer electronics means immunity requirements also apply.
regulatory.designImpact: PCB layout must minimise switching noise from solar PMIC and NPU; shielding strategy for NPU SoC must be defined; cable routing (if any external cables) must be filtered. Steel body variant provides inherent shielding but radome apertures re-open emission paths. Ceramic body requires explicit EMC shielding layer or compartment around NPU/PMIC.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: EMC test report (radiated and conducted emissions + immunity) from UKAS-accredited lab; UKCA Declaration of Conformity referencing BS EN 55032 (emissions) and BS EN 55035 (immunity) or equivalent harmonised standards.
regulatory.gapAction: Define body material (steel vs ceramic) as this determines shielding strategy; include EMC test scope in RF test house brief; conduct pre-compliance scan on prototype PCB before formal submission.

regulatory.name: General Product Safety Regulations 2005 (SI 2005/1803) — GPSR
regulatory.summary: UK statutory baseline requiring all consumer products placed on the market to be safe; applies where no sector-specific statutory instrument covers the full safety scope.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — Consumer-facing garden product sold direct-to-consumer and through retail; GPSR applies as the safety backstop across both solar-only and mains variants, covering mechanical hazards (perch, reservoir interchange, mounting hardware), thermal hazards (battery, solar panel), and any residual risks not addressed by sector-specific regulations.
regulatory.designImpact: Risk assessment must cover mechanical injury from mounting hardware and perch load cell, thermal runaway containment of LiFePO4 battery, ingress protection for outdoor use (minimum IP54 body, IP65 sensor apertures as flagged in report), and child/pet interaction with seed reservoirs and electrical apertures.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: Product risk assessment document; instructions for safe use in multiple languages (English mandatory for UK); incident reporting procedure in place; UK Responsible Person appointed and contact details on product/packaging.
regulatory.gapAction: Commission product risk assessment covering all identified hazard categories; draft safe-use instructions; appoint UK Responsible Person.

regulatory.name: UK Conformity Assessed (UKCA) Marking Requirements
regulatory.summary: UK post-Brexit conformity marking scheme replacing CE marking for products placed on the Great Britain market; required for products covered by one or more of the new UK product regulations.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — Entire Hedgerow product placed on the GB market; UKCA marking is required under the Electrical Equipment (Safety) Regulations 2016, Radio Equipment Regulations 2017, and EMC Regulations 2016. CE marking alone is no longer sufficient for GB market placement (transition period ended 31 December 2024 for most categories).
regulatory.designImpact: Technical file must be compiled and held by the UK Responsible Person; conformity assessment route (self-declaration vs third-party) depends on which harmonised standards are used and whether radio equipment essential requirements are fully covered by harmonised standards. UKCA mark must appear on product and packaging with UK Responsible Person address.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: UKCA Declaration of Conformity covering all applicable regulations; technical construction file; UK Responsible Person appointment letter; UKCA mark artwork applied to product label and packaging.
regulatory.gapAction: Appoint UK Responsible Person; compile technical file structure; confirm conformity assessment route for each applicable regulation; add UKCA mark to label and packaging artwork.

regulatory.code: Waste Electrical and Electronic Equipment Regulations 2013
regulatory.name: Waste Electrical and Electronic Equipment Regulations 2013 (SI 2013/3113) — WEEE
regulatory.summary: UK statutory instrument requiring producers of electrical and electronic equipment to register, finance collection, and meet recycling/recovery targets for end-of-life products.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — Hedgerow is an electrical and electronic product placed on the UK consumer market; producer registration with a UK-approved WEEE compliance scheme is mandatory before first sale. The LiFePO4 battery is separately subject to battery waste regulations.
regulatory.designImpact: Product must be designed for disassembly to enable battery removal for separate collection; WEEE crossed-bin symbol must appear on product and packaging; battery must be user-removable or service-removable per battery waste regulations.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: WEEE producer registration number from a UK-approved compliance scheme (e.g. Valpak, Recolight); evidence of scheme membership and annual reporting; crossed-bin symbol on product label.
regulatory.gapAction: Register with a UK WEEE compliance scheme before first product sale; confirm battery removal procedure in design; add crossed-bin symbol to label artwork.

regulatory.code: Batteries and Accumulators (Placing on the Market) Regulations 2008
regulatory.name: Batteries and Accumulators (Placing on the Market) Regulations 2008 (SI 2008/2164) as amended
regulatory.summary: UK statutory instrument controlling the placing on the market of batteries, requiring producer registration, labelling, and end-of-life take-back for batteries placed on the UK market.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — LiFePO4 battery pack integrated into Hedgerow; the producer (Hedgerow manufacturer/importer) must register as a battery producer and ensure the battery carries the crossed-bin symbol and capacity marking. Note: the UK Batteries Regulation 2023 updates are in progress — monitor DEFRA guidance.
regulatory.designImpact: Battery must be labelled with crossed-bin symbol and chemical composition (LiFePO4 / Li-Fe); battery must be removable by end user or at a service point to enable separate collection; battery capacity (Wh) must be declared on packaging.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: Battery producer registration with UK Environment Agency or approved compliance scheme; battery labelling compliance evidence; take-back scheme documentation.
regulatory.gapAction: Register as battery producer with UK Environment Agency; confirm battery labelling requirements with compliance scheme; design battery compartment for tool-free or single-tool removal.

regulatory.name: UN Manual of Tests and Criteria, Part III, Sub-section 38.3 — Lithium Batteries
regulatory.summary: Mandatory transport safety test series for lithium cells and batteries; required before any road, sea, or air shipment of lithium battery cells or assembled packs.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — LiFePO4 battery cells and assembled pack during inbound supply chain transport and outbound distribution to consumers; UN 38.3 is mandated by the Carriage of Dangerous Goods and Use of Transportable Pressure Equipment Regulations 2009 (CDG Regs) for road, IMDG Code for sea, and IATA DGR for air freight.
regulatory.designImpact: Battery pack design (cell count, configuration, BMS protection) must be finalised before transport testing; any design change to cell type, pack configuration, or BMS after certification requires re-testing. BMS must include overcharge, over-discharge, and short-circuit protection to pass tests T5 and T6.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: UN 38.3 test summary report from cell supplier or accredited test laboratory covering the specific cell type and pack configuration used in Hedgerow; ADR dangerous goods documentation for road shipment of battery stock.
regulatory.gapAction: Confirm cell supplier holds valid UN 38.3 certification for the selected LiFePO4 cell; if pack configuration differs from certified configuration, commission pack-level UN 38.3 testing; prepare ADR documentation template for logistics team.

regulatory.name: Safety requirements for portable sealed secondary lithium cells and batteries for use in portable applications — Part 2: Lithium systems
regulatory.summary: Harmonised standard for safety of lithium battery packs in portable/consumer applications; demonstrates compliance with Electrical Equipment (Safety) Regulations 2016 for the battery subsystem.
regulatory.applicability: UK designated standard — LiFePO4 battery pack within Hedgerow (consumer portable application); demonstrates compliance with the Electrical Equipment (Safety) Regulations 2016 for the battery subsystem. If the battery is classified as an industrial/stationary system, BS EN IEC 62619 applies instead — classification depends on final Wh capacity and application definition.
regulatory.designImpact: Battery pack must pass cell-level and pack-level abuse tests (overcharge, forced discharge, short circuit, crush, thermal abuse); BMS protection thresholds must be set to prevent conditions that would trigger test failures; pack enclosure must contain any cell venting without propagation.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: BS EN IEC 62133-2 test report from UKAS-accredited or internationally recognised lab for the specific cell type and pack configuration; supplier declaration or type-test certificate.
regulatory.gapAction: Determine whether battery pack falls under BS EN IEC 62133-2 (consumer portable) or BS EN IEC 62619 (industrial); obtain cell supplier's existing test report and assess whether pack-level testing is additionally required.

regulatory.name: Audio/video, information and communication technology equipment — Part 1: Safety requirements
regulatory.summary: Harmonised standard for safety of AV/ICT equipment; the primary safety standard for the NPU SoC, camera module, and associated electronics in Hedgerow.
regulatory.applicability: UK designated standard — NPU SoC, camera module, power management PCBA, and associated electronics; demonstrates compliance with the Electrical Equipment (Safety) Regulations 2016 for the electronics subsystem. Replaces BS EN 60950-1 and BS EN 60065 for ICT/AV equipment.
regulatory.designImpact: Creepage and clearance distances, insulation coordination, and thermal limits for the electronics assembly must meet BS EN 62368-1 requirements; mains-powered variant must meet reinforced insulation between mains and SELV circuits; outdoor enclosure must provide adequate protection against ingress (IP rating feeds into this standard's environmental requirements).
regulatory.evidenceRequired: BS EN 62368-1 test report or self-declaration with supporting technical file from UKAS-accredited lab or competent internal test; included in UKCA technical file.
regulatory.gapAction: Include BS EN 62368-1 scope in electronics design review; engage test house to confirm applicability and test scope for both solar-only and mains variants.

regulatory.name: Short Range Devices (SRD) operating in the frequency range 25 MHz to 1 000 MHz — Part 1/2
regulatory.summary: ETSI harmonised standard for LoRa 868 MHz ISM band short-range devices; demonstrates compliance with Radio Equipment Regulations 2017 spectrum efficiency essential requirement.
regulatory.applicability: UK designated standard — LoRa 868 MHz mesh radio between multiple Hedgerow feeders; demonstrates compliance with Radio Equipment Regulations 2017 for the LoRa radio path. UK 868 MHz ISM band duty cycle limits (1% or sub-band specific) apply and must be respected in firmware.
regulatory.designImpact: LoRa firmware must implement duty cycle management to stay within UK 868 MHz sub-band limits; antenna gain and EIRP must not exceed permitted levels; antenna placement must achieve ≥86 mm separation from Wi-Fi and cellular antennas to avoid desense.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: BS EN 300 220 test report for the LoRa module at system level (or pre-certified module test report plus integration assessment); included in UKCA technical file under Radio Equipment Regulations 2017.
regulatory.gapAction: Select pre-certified LoRa module with BS EN 300 220 certification; confirm duty cycle management is implemented in firmware; include LoRa antenna placement in RF test house brief.

regulatory.code: Product Security and Telecommunications Infrastructure Act 2022
regulatory.name: Product Security and Telecommunications Infrastructure Act 2022 (PSTI Act) — Part 1
regulatory.summary: UK statutory requirement for consumer connectable products to meet minimum cybersecurity requirements; mandatory from 29 April 2024.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — Hedgerow is a consumer connectable product (Wi-Fi, optional cellular, LoRa); PSTI Part 1 applies from 29 April 2024. All three connectivity paths (Wi-Fi, cellular, LoRa) bring the product within scope. The companion app and cloud backend are in scope insofar as they interact with the connectable product.
regulatory.designImpact: No universal default passwords permitted — each unit must have a unique default credential or require user-set password on first use; a published vulnerability disclosure policy (VDP) must be in place; minimum security update support period must be declared to consumers; software bill of materials (SBOM) discipline required to track component vulnerabilities.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: Statement of compliance with PSTI Regulations 2023 (the secondary legislation); published vulnerability disclosure policy URL; declaration of minimum security support period on product packaging or in-box documentation; UK Responsible Person appointment (shared with UKCA obligations).
regulatory.gapAction: Implement unique per-device credential generation in firmware; publish vulnerability disclosure policy on company website; declare minimum security update period on packaging; review companion app authentication against PSTI requirements.

regulatory.name: UK General Data Protection Regulation and Data Protection Act 2018
regulatory.summary: UK data protection law governing the collection, processing, and storage of personal data; the camera, microphone, and individual-bird identification features may incidentally capture personal data (images of people, audio).
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — Camera (12 MP with optical zoom) and microphone sensors may capture images or audio of people in or adjacent to the garden; individual identification and citizen-science data contribution features process data that could be linked to individuals (garden location, behavioural patterns). UK GDPR applies to any personal data processed by the companion app or cloud backend.
regulatory.designImpact: Privacy-by-design required: camera field of view and zoom capability must be considered in the context of neighbour privacy; on-device processing (rather than cloud upload of raw video) reduces but does not eliminate data protection obligations; citizen-science contribution toggle must be genuinely opt-in with clear consent; data retention periods must be defined and enforced in the app.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: Data Protection Impact Assessment (DPIA) for camera/microphone data processing; ICO registration (if required); privacy notice published and accessible from companion app; consent mechanism for citizen-science data contribution; data processing agreement with BTO.
regulatory.gapAction: Commission DPIA covering camera, microphone, location, and citizen-science data flows; draft privacy notice and consent mechanism for app; establish data processing agreement with BTO before citizen-science feature launch.

regulatory.name: Restriction of the Use of Certain Hazardous Substances in Electrical and Electronic Equipment Regulations 2012 (SI 2012/3032) — UK RoHS
regulatory.summary: UK statutory instrument restricting hazardous substances (lead, mercury, cadmium, hexavalent chromium, PBB, PBDE, and four phthalates) in electrical and electronic equipment.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — Hedgerow PCBAs, solder, cable insulation, and electronic components; applies to all electrical and electronic equipment placed on the UK market. Powder-coated steel body and ceramic body are unlikely to contain restricted substances but must be confirmed with suppliers.
regulatory.designImpact: PCB assembly must use lead-free solder (Sn-Ag-Cu or equivalent); component selection must exclude restricted substances; supplier declarations of conformity (DoC) required for all electronic components and sub-assemblies.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: RoHS Declaration of Conformity; supplier RoHS DoCs for all electronic components; technical documentation demonstrating substance levels are below maximum concentration values.
regulatory.gapAction: Include RoHS compliance requirement in component procurement specification; collect supplier RoHS DoCs during BOM finalisation; add RoHS DoC to UKCA technical file.

regulatory.name: Degrees of Protection Provided by Enclosures (IP Code)
regulatory.summary: Standard defining ingress protection ratings for enclosures against solid particles and liquids; the IP rating of Hedgerow's enclosure determines its fitness for permanent outdoor garden installation.
regulatory.applicability: UK designated standard — Outdoor garden installation in UK weather conditions (rain, frost, condensation); IP rating underpins compliance with the Electrical Equipment (Safety) Regulations 2016 and GPSR for outdoor electrical products. Report recommends minimum IP54 for body and IP65 for sensor/connector apertures — these must be formally tested and declared.
regulatory.designImpact: Enclosure design must achieve at least IP54 (dust protected, splash-proof from all directions) for the main body and IP65 (dust-tight, jet-proof) for sensor ports, camera window, microphone port, and connector apertures. Drainage paths, gasket selection, and cable entry glands must all be designed and tested to the declared IP rating. Modular reservoir interchange mechanism must not compromise the IP rating of the electronics enclosure.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: IP test report from UKAS-accredited test house confirming declared IP rating for the production enclosure design; IP rating marked on product label.
regulatory.gapAction: Define target IP rating (minimum IP54 body / IP65 apertures) in product specification; design gaskets, drainage, and cable entries to achieve target; commission IP test on first production-representative prototype.

regulatory.name: Assessment of the compliance of low power electronic and electrical equipment with the basic restrictions related to human exposure to electromagnetic fields (10 MHz – 300 GHz)
regulatory.summary: Simplified assessment standard for RF exposure (SAR/power density) for low-power radio devices; demonstrates compliance with Radio Equipment Regulations 2017 health and safety essential requirement for RF exposure.
regulatory.applicability: UK designated standard — Wi-Fi (2.4/5 GHz), cellular (LTE-M/NB-IoT), and LoRa (868 MHz) radio transmitters; demonstrates compliance with Radio Equipment Regulations 2017 Article 3(1)(a) health and safety essential requirement for RF exposure. Garden-mounted product is not body-worn but proximity to users during seed refilling must be assessed.
regulatory.designImpact: Transmit power levels for all radio paths must be confirmed to fall within BS EN 62479 simplified assessment limits; if any radio path exceeds simplified assessment thresholds, full SAR testing per BS EN 50663 or BS EN 62209 is required. Antenna placement relative to likely user hand positions during seed refilling must be considered.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: BS EN 62479 simplified assessment calculation or test report for all radio paths; included in UKCA technical file under Radio Equipment Regulations 2017.
regulatory.gapAction: Obtain transmit power specifications for all selected radio modules; perform BS EN 62479 simplified assessment calculation; if any path fails simplified assessment, commission full SAR test.

regulatory.name: Electricity at Work Regulations 1989 (EAWR) (SI 1989/635)
regulatory.summary: UK statutory instrument imposing duties on persons who design, construct, and maintain electrical systems to prevent danger; applies to the design of the mains-powered variant.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — Mains-powered variant design and any installation involving connection to the domestic mains supply; EAWR imposes duties on the designer to ensure the electrical system is constructed so as to prevent danger. Relevant to the design of the mains input circuit, earthing, and fault protection.
regulatory.designImpact: Mains input circuit must include appropriate fusing, earthing (Class I or Class II decision required), and fault current protection; design must prevent danger from electric shock, burn, fire, and explosion under both normal and fault conditions.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: Design review record demonstrating EAWR compliance; for mains variant, electrical safety test report (dielectric strength, earth continuity, leakage current) as part of BS EN 62368-1 type testing.
regulatory.gapAction: Confirm Class I vs Class II construction decision for mains variant; include EAWR compliance review in electrical design sign-off process; ensure mains variant electrical safety tests are included in BS EN 62368-1 test scope.

regulatory.name: Electrical Equipment (Safety) Regulations 2016 (SI 2016/1101)
regulatory.summary: UK statutory instrument implementing the Low Voltage Directive for electrical equipment operating between 50–1000 V AC or 75–1500 V DC; requires UKCA marking and a technical file.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — The complete BESS unit (PCS AC output, internal LV distribution, BMS, auxiliary supplies) falls within the LV scope; UKCA marking is mandatory before placing on the UK market. Designated standards BS EN IEC 62933-5-2 and BS EN IEC 62619/63056 are the primary conformity route.
regulatory.designImpact: A technical file must be compiled covering design, risk assessment, test evidence, and instructions; UKCA mark and UK-authorised representative declaration of conformity required on the container nameplate before first delivery.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: Declaration of Conformity referencing UKCA scheme; technical construction file; test reports from UKAS-accredited laboratory against designated standards; UK Authorised Representative appointment letter.
regulatory.gapAction: Appoint a UK Authorised Representative and open a technical file; confirm which UKAS-accredited test house will conduct system-level testing against BS EN IEC 62933-5-2.

regulatory.name: UK Conformity Assessed (UKCA) Marking — Product Safety and Metrology etc. (Amendment etc.) (EU Exit) Regulations 2019 and successor instruments
regulatory.summary: Umbrella UK market-access scheme replacing CE marking; mandatory for electrical, machinery, EMC, and radio products placed on the GB market.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — Applies to the complete BESS unit as an electrical/machinery product placed on the GB market; CE marking alone is no longer accepted for new GB placements.
regulatory.designImpact: UKCA mark must appear on the container nameplate alongside rated voltage, current, energy capacity, and manufacturer details; conformity must be assessed against UK-designated standards before first shipment.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: UKCA Declaration of Conformity; technical file index; conformity assessment records referencing UK-designated standards; UK Responsible Person details.
regulatory.gapAction: Confirm UKCA conformity route (self-declaration vs. third-party notified body) and integrate UKCA marking into nameplate design and documentation pack.

regulatory.name: Electromagnetic Compatibility Regulations 2016 (SI 2016/1091)
regulatory.summary: UK statutory instrument requiring electrical and electronic apparatus to not cause harmful electromagnetic interference and to have adequate immunity.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — The PCS (1.5 MW bi-directional inverter), BMS electronics, SCADA gateway, and auxiliary controls all generate and are susceptible to electromagnetic disturbance; UKCA marking under EMC is required.
regulatory.designImpact: PCS and control electronics must meet conducted and radiated emission limits and immunity levels per BS EN IEC 61000 series; shielding, filtering, and cable segregation strategy must be documented in the technical file.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: EMC test report from UKAS-accredited laboratory against BS EN IEC 61000-6-2 (immunity, industrial) and BS EN IEC 61000-6-4 (emissions, industrial); EMC Declaration of Conformity.
regulatory.gapAction: Confirm PCS supplier holds valid EMC test reports for the 1.5 MW inverter; if not, schedule EMC testing at UKAS-accredited facility and add to technical file.

regulatory.name: Electricity at Work Regulations 1989 (EAWR)
regulatory.summary: UK statutory instrument imposing duties on employers and the self-employed to ensure electrical systems are constructed, maintained, and operated safely.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — Applies to the fixed electrical installation inside the container (DC busbars, AC distribution, protection coordination, isolation) and to all work activities on the energised system during installation, commissioning, and maintenance.
regulatory.designImpact: All electrical systems must be designed to prevent danger; isolation and lock-off provisions, protection coordination, and safe working procedures must be documented; competent persons must carry out all electrical work.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: Electrical installation certificate (EIC) signed by a competent person; schedule of inspections and test results; written safe system of work for energisation and commissioning.
regulatory.gapAction: Engage a qualified electrical engineer to design internal distribution to BS 7671 and produce an EIC after installation; draft energisation safe system of work before first commissioning.

regulatory.name: Requirements for Electrical Installations (IET Wiring Regulations, 18th Edition)
regulatory.summary: UK wiring regulations governing the design, installation, and verification of fixed electrical installations; de facto enforcement standard for EAWR compliance.
regulatory.applicability: UK designated standard — Internal LV wiring, protection devices, earthing, and isolation within the container; demonstrates compliance with the Electricity at Work Regulations 1989. Amendment 2 (2022) requirements for energy storage apply directly.
regulatory.designImpact: Internal distribution must comply with shock protection (ADS), earthing arrangements, overcurrent and fault protection, isolation and switching, and cable sizing; Section 722 (electric vehicle charging) and emerging storage guidance in Amendment 2 inform battery room wiring requirements.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: Electrical Installation Certificate (EIC) with schedule of inspections and test results, signed by a competent person registered with a Part P/ECA-recognised scheme or equivalent.
regulatory.gapAction: Design internal distribution board, cable sizing, and protection coordination to BS 7671 Amendment 2; engage qualified electrician to inspect, test, and issue EIC after container installation on site.

regulatory.name: Electricity Safety, Quality and Continuity Regulations 2002 (SI 2002/2665, as amended)
regulatory.summary: UK statutory instrument governing the safety and quality of electricity supply networks; underpins DNO requirements for grid-connected generation and storage.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — The BESS connects in parallel with the public distribution network; ESQCR imposes obligations on the network operator and, via G99, on the owner of the generating/storage plant. The G99 application process is the primary compliance mechanism.
regulatory.designImpact: PCS must meet voltage and frequency limits, power quality requirements, and protection settings mandated by the DNO under ESQCR; islanding prevention and automatic disconnection on loss of mains must be implemented.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: G99 commissioning test record countersigned by the host DNO; generation connection agreement; protection relay settings schedule accepted by DNO.
regulatory.gapAction: Initiate G99 application with the host DNO at the earliest opportunity; confirm protection relay type and settings with DNO before PCS procurement is finalised.

regulatory.name: ENA Engineering Recommendation G99 — Requirements for the Connection of Generation Equipment in Parallel with Public Distribution Networks above 16 A per Phase
regulatory.summary: Mandatory UK grid code for storage systems connecting in parallel with the distribution network above 16 A per phase; enforced by every DNO under ESQCR.
regulatory.applicability: UK approved code — Grid connection point for the 1.5 MW / G99-rated BESS; ENA G99 is the Engineering Recommendation enforced by all UK DNOs, sitting under ESQCR 2002. Grid-forming capability and ride-through parameters are explicitly required.
regulatory.designImpact: PCS must support grid-forming mode, loss-of-mains (LoM) protection (ROCOF and vector shift), frequency and voltage ride-through per G99 Annex, and remote trip capability; protection settings must be agreed with the DNO before commissioning.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: G99 Type Test certificate for the PCS (or equivalent accepted by DNO); G99 commissioning test record signed by host DNO; generation connection agreement; protection relay settings schedule.
regulatory.gapAction: Submit G99 application to host DNO; confirm PCS supplier holds a valid G99 Type Test certificate; schedule DNO witness commissioning test within the two-day commissioning window.

regulatory.name: Electrical energy storage (EES) systems — Part 5-2: Safety requirements for grid-integrated electrical energy storage systems
regulatory.summary: UK-designated harmonised standard for stationary battery energy storage safety at system level; primary conformity route for UKCA marking under the Electrical Equipment (Safety) Regulations 2016.
regulatory.applicability: UK designated standard — Complete BESS enclosure including LFP racks, PCS, BMS, thermal management, and fire system; demonstrates compliance with the Electrical Equipment (Safety) Regulations 2016 for UKCA marking. Covers thermal runaway propagation, fire containment, ventilation, and electrical safety at system level.
regulatory.designImpact: System must pass thermal runaway propagation tests, fire containment and suppression integration tests, ventilation adequacy assessment, and electrical isolation/protection tests; deflagration vent area and burst pressure calculations required; fire detection and suppression system must be integrated and tested as part of the system.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: Test report from UKAS-accredited laboratory demonstrating compliance with BS EN IEC 62933-5-2 at system level; included in UKCA technical file.
regulatory.gapAction: Identify UKAS-accredited test house capable of BS EN IEC 62933-5-2 system-level testing; scope the test programme with the integrator and build test schedule into the product development timeline.

regulatory.name: Secondary cells and batteries containing alkaline or other non-acid electrolytes — Safety requirements for secondary lithium cells and batteries for use in industrial applications
regulatory.summary: UK-designated standard for safety of lithium cells and battery modules in industrial applications; applies at cell and module level within the BESS.
regulatory.applicability: UK designated standard — LFP cells and battery modules within the racks; demonstrates compliance with the Electrical Equipment (Safety) Regulations 2016 at cell/module level. Cited in the research report as the required cell standard.
regulatory.designImpact: Cells and modules must pass abuse tests (overcharge, over-discharge, short circuit, crush, thermal abuse); BMS must implement the protection functions specified in the standard; cell supplier must provide conformity evidence.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: BS EN IEC 62619 test report or certificate from cell/module supplier; supplier declaration of conformity; include in UKCA technical file.
regulatory.gapAction: Request BS EN IEC 62619 test reports and declaration of conformity from the LFP cell/module supplier during procurement; verify reports cover the specific cell format and chemistry selected.

regulatory.name: Secondary cells and batteries containing alkaline or other non-acid electrolytes — Safety requirements for secondary lithium cells and batteries for use in electrical energy storage systems
regulatory.summary: UK-designated standard extending BS EN IEC 62619 to battery systems (multi-module assemblies) used in stationary energy storage applications.
regulatory.applicability: UK designated standard — Battery rack assemblies and the complete battery system within the BESS; demonstrates compliance with the Electrical Equipment (Safety) Regulations 2016 at system/rack level. Cited in the research report as required alongside BS EN IEC 62619.
regulatory.designImpact: Rack-level and system-level battery assemblies must meet additional safety requirements beyond cell level, including inter-module protection, communication with BMS, and system-level abuse tolerance; rack mechanical design must accommodate test requirements.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: BS EN IEC 63056 test report or certificate for the rack/system assembly; supplier or integrator declaration of conformity; include in UKCA technical file.
regulatory.gapAction: Confirm with the battery rack supplier whether BS EN IEC 63056 certification exists for the selected rack configuration; if not, scope additional testing as part of the system qualification programme.

regulatory.name: UN Manual of Tests and Criteria, Part III, Sub-section 38.3 — Lithium metal and lithium ion batteries
regulatory.summary: Mandatory transport safety test protocol for lithium cells and batteries; required before any road, sea, or air shipment of lithium battery modules.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — LFP cell modules and battery racks during road transport from manufacturer/integrator to UK site; UN 38.3 underpins the Carriage of Dangerous Goods and Use of Transportable Pressure Equipment Regulations 2009 (CDG 2009) and ADR for road transport. Also required for any sea freight under IMDG Code.
regulatory.designImpact: All LFP cells and battery modules must have passed altitude simulation, thermal cycling, vibration, shock, overcharge, forced discharge, and impact/crush tests before transport; transport documentation (dangerous goods note, ADR consignment note) must reference valid UN 38.3 summary report.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: UN 38.3 test summary report from cell/module supplier or accredited laboratory; ADR dangerous goods consignment note for road transport; IMDG documentation if sea freight is used.
regulatory.gapAction: Confirm cell and module supplier holds a current UN 38.3 test summary report covering the specific cell format; prepare ADR transport documentation before first road shipment of battery modules.

regulatory.name: Supply of Machinery (Safety) Regulations 2008 (SI 2008/1597, as amended)
regulatory.summary: UK statutory instrument implementing the Machinery Directive for machinery placed on the UK market; applies to automated and power-driven equipment with moving parts.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — The liquid cooling skid (pump, fan, chiller compressor), automated fire suppression actuators, and any motorised switchgear within the BESS constitute machinery under the Regulations; UKCA marking under the Machinery scheme is required for these sub-assemblies if supplied as standalone units, or the integrator must address machinery hazards in the system technical file.
regulatory.designImpact: Risk assessment to BS EN ISO 12100 required for all machinery elements; guarding, emergency stop, and isolation provisions must be designed in; cooling skid must meet relevant machinery safety standards.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: Machinery Declaration of Conformity for the cooling skid and any motorised sub-assemblies; risk assessment to BS EN ISO 12100; include in UKCA technical file.
regulatory.gapAction: Confirm cooling skid supplier holds a valid Machinery Declaration of Conformity; if the integrator assembles the skid, commission a BS EN ISO 12100 risk assessment and prepare machinery technical file section.

regulatory.name: Pressure Systems Safety Regulations 2000 (PSSR 2000, SI 2000/128)
regulatory.summary: UK statutory instrument governing the safe design, installation, and operation of pressure systems containing relevant fluids; applies to the liquid cooling circuit once installed on site.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — The glycol/water liquid cooling circuit (pipework, pump, chiller, expansion vessel, pressure relief) constitutes a pressure system under PSSR 2000 once installed and in service on the customer's site; the site operator becomes the duty holder.
regulatory.designImpact: Cooling circuit must be designed with appropriate pressure relief, isolation, and drainage; a written scheme of examination must be prepared by a competent person before the system is brought into service; operating and maintenance instructions must address pressure system safety.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: Written scheme of examination prepared by a competent person (e.g., insurance engineer); pressure test records for the cooling circuit; operating instructions referencing PSSR duties for the site operator.
regulatory.gapAction: Engage a competent person (insurance engineer or equivalent) to prepare a written scheme of examination for the cooling circuit; include PSSR obligations in the site operator handover documentation.

regulatory.name: Construction (Design and Management) Regulations 2015 (SI 2015/51)
regulatory.summary: UK statutory instrument imposing duties on clients, designers, and contractors for health and safety in construction projects; applies to the site installation of the BESS.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — Installation of the BESS on a prepared concrete pad, including foundation anchorage, AC tie-in, and commissioning, constitutes construction work under CDM 2015; the site client, principal designer, and principal contractor all have statutory duties.
regulatory.designImpact: Pre-construction health and safety information must be provided to the principal contractor; a construction phase plan must be prepared; the health and safety file must be handed over to the client on completion; lifting operations (crane/HIAB for 25–40 t container) require a lifting plan under LOLER 1998.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: Construction phase plan; health and safety file; LOLER lifting plan and crane/HIAB inspection records; principal contractor and principal designer appointment letters.
regulatory.gapAction: Confirm whether the project triggers the CDM notifiable threshold (>30 working days with >20 workers, or >500 person-days); appoint principal designer and principal contractor; prepare pre-construction health and safety information pack for site installation.

regulatory.code: Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974
regulatory.name: Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974 (HSWA)
regulatory.summary: Primary UK health and safety legislation imposing general duties on employers, the self-employed, and manufacturers to ensure safety of persons at work and affected by work activities.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — Applies to all work activities associated with manufacturing, installing, commissioning, and maintaining the BESS; the founder as manufacturer has duties under Section 6 (safe design, testing, information provision) in addition to employer duties.
regulatory.designImpact: Section 6 duty requires the founder to ensure the BESS is designed and constructed to be safe when used as intended; adequate information (installation manual, commissioning procedure, maintenance schedule, emergency response plan) must be provided with every unit.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: Section 6 safety information pack (installation manual, commissioning procedure, maintenance schedule, emergency response plan); risk assessments for foreseeable use and misuse scenarios; records of design verification and testing.
regulatory.gapAction: Compile a Section 6 information pack covering installation, commissioning, normal operation, maintenance, and emergency response; ensure it is reviewed by a competent safety professional before first delivery.

regulatory.name: National Fire Chiefs Council — Fire Safety Guidance for Grid Scale Battery Energy Storage Systems (2020, updated 2023)
regulatory.summary: NFCC operational guidance used by UK fire and rescue services, local planning authorities, and insurers when assessing BESS fire risk; not statutory but treated as the de facto standard by AHJs.
regulatory.applicability: UK approved code — Fire safety design and planning for the containerised BESS on UK sites; NFCC guidance is referenced by local planning authorities and fire and rescue services as the benchmark for acceptable fire risk management. Cited explicitly in the project brief.
regulatory.designImpact: Minimum 3 m separation from property lines, occupied buildings, and other ESS units; emergency services access on at least one long side; fire detection (smoke, heat, VOC/off-gas) and suppression integrated and tested; thermal runaway propagation prevention demonstrated (UL 9540A or equivalent test data); fire strategy document required for planning.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: Fire strategy document referencing NFCC guidance; thermal runaway propagation test data (UL 9540A or equivalent); fire detection and suppression commissioning certificate; confirmation of separation distances from site layout drawing; fire and rescue service pre-application consultation record.
regulatory.gapAction: Engage a fire safety engineer to prepare a fire strategy document aligned with NFCC guidance; confirm separation distances on the site layout drawing; initiate pre-application consultation with the local fire and rescue service.

regulatory.name: NFPA 855 — Standard for the Installation of Stationary Energy Storage Systems (2023 Edition)
regulatory.summary: US reference standard for stationary ESS installation; not UK statutory but widely cited by UK insurers and NFCC guidance as a design reference for fire safety and spacing.
regulatory.applicability: Voluntary reference — Fire safety design and insurer underwriting; NFPA 855 is not UK statute but is cited in the project brief and by NFCC guidance and commercial insurers as a reference for deflagration venting, suppression system design, and separation distances. UK statutory peer is BS EN IEC 62933-5-2 and NFCC guidance.
regulatory.designImpact: Deflagration vent area calculation and burst pressure design for the container; suppression system density and agent selection; spacing and separation concepts inform site layout, but UK compliance is demonstrated via BS EN IEC 62933-5-2 and NFCC guidance.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: Not mandated; insurer may request an NFPA 855 alignment statement or gap analysis; deflagration vent calculation to be included in the fire strategy document.
regulatory.gapAction: Review NFPA 855 Chapter 4 (ESS installation) and incorporate deflagration vent and suppression requirements into the fire strategy document; prepare an alignment statement for the commercial insurer.

regulatory.name: UL 9540A — Test Method for Evaluating Thermal Runaway Fire Propagation in Battery Energy Storage Systems
regulatory.summary: US test method for evaluating thermal runaway propagation at cell, module, unit, and installation level; referenced by NFCC guidance and insurers as evidence of fire propagation control.
regulatory.applicability: Voluntary reference — Thermal runaway propagation evidence for NFCC fire strategy and insurer underwriting; UL 9540A is not UK statute but is the test method cited by NFCC guidance and commercial insurers to demonstrate that thermal runaway does not propagate between modules or racks. UK statutory peer for system-level fire safety is BS EN IEC 62933-5-2.
regulatory.designImpact: Battery rack and module design must prevent thermal runaway propagation between cells and between modules; UL 9540A test data at module and system level informs the fire strategy and suppression system design; cell-level abuse test data required.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: UL 9540A test report at module level and system/installation level from the battery rack supplier or an accredited laboratory; include in fire strategy document and UKCA technical file.
regulatory.gapAction: Request UL 9540A test reports from the battery rack supplier; if not available, scope UL 9540A testing as part of the system qualification programme and include in the fire strategy document.

regulatory.name: ISO 1496-1 — Series 1 freight containers — Specification and testing — Part 1: General cargo containers for general purposes
regulatory.summary: Container structural certification standard; the original CSC plate is voided once the container shell is structurally modified by vents, large openings, or internal reinforcements.
regulatory.applicability: Voluntary reference — Shipping container enclosure structural integrity; the original CSC plate is voided once the container shell is structurally modified (deflagration vents, HVAC penetrations, cable gland plates, internal rack bracing). Re-certification via alternative structural analysis is required; ISO 1496-1 itself is not UK statute.
regulatory.designImpact: Original CSC plate voided by structural modifications; design must rely on alternative structural certification (FEA to BS EN 1993 or classification-society inspection); foundation anchorage design must account for actual corner casting loads up to ~10 t per corner.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: Finite element analysis report to BS EN 1993 or new structural certification from a recognised classification society or structural engineer; include in technical file and provide to site structural engineer for foundation design.
regulatory.gapAction: Commission a structural analysis of the modified container under design loads (wind, seismic if applicable, internal pressure from deflagration venting); engage a structural engineer or classification society to certify the modified enclosure.

regulatory.name: ISO 1161 — Series 1 freight containers — Corner fittings — Specification
regulatory.summary: Dimensional and strength standard for ISO corner castings used for lifting, stacking, and foundation anchorage of the container.
regulatory.applicability: Voluntary reference — Foundation anchorage and lifting interface; ISO 1161 corner castings are the structural interface for M24/M30 foundation anchors and four-point crane lift; compliance with ISO 1161 geometry is required for standard spreader bar and twist-lock compatibility.
regulatory.designImpact: Foundation anchor bolt pattern and pad design must be coordinated with ISO 1161 corner casting geometry; lifting plan must specify a four-point spreader bar rated for up to 40 t; corner casting condition must be inspected before each lift.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: Structural engineer's foundation design referencing ISO 1161 corner casting loads; LOLER lifting plan referencing ISO 1161 geometry and rated capacity; corner casting inspection record.
regulatory.gapAction: Provide ISO 1161 corner casting load data to the site structural engineer for foundation pad design; include corner casting inspection in the pre-lift checklist within the LOLER lifting plan.

regulatory.code: Batteries and Accumulators (Placing on the Market) Regulations 2008
regulatory.name: Batteries and Accumulators (Placing on the Market) Regulations 2008 (SI 2008/2164, as amended for GB)
regulatory.summary: UK statutory instrument controlling the placing on the market of batteries and accumulators; imposes labelling, registration, and take-back obligations.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — LFP battery modules and the complete battery system placed on the GB market; the Regulations require batteries to be labelled with the crossed-out wheelie bin symbol, capacity, and chemical composition; producer registration with a compliance scheme is required.
regulatory.designImpact: Battery modules and the system must carry the crossed-out wheelie bin label and capacity marking; the founder must register as a battery producer with an approved compliance scheme (e.g., Valpak, Ecosurety) before first sale.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: Battery producer registration certificate from an approved compliance scheme; labelling compliance evidence on battery modules and system documentation.
regulatory.gapAction: Register as a battery producer with a UK-approved compliance scheme before first unit is placed on the market; confirm labelling requirements are met on battery module and system nameplates.

regulatory.name: Waste Electrical and Electronic Equipment Regulations 2013 (SI 2013/3113, as amended for GB)
regulatory.summary: UK statutory instrument requiring producers of electrical and electronic equipment to finance the collection, treatment, and recycling of waste EEE; applies to the BESS as a large-scale EEE product.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — The complete BESS unit (PCS, BMS, SCADA, auxiliary electronics) placed on the GB market; the founder must register as a WEEE producer and join an approved compliance scheme before first sale.
regulatory.designImpact: Product must be designed for disassembly and recycling where practicable; WEEE producer registration number must appear in product documentation; end-of-life take-back obligations must be communicated to customers.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: WEEE producer registration certificate from an approved compliance scheme; evidence of WEEE obligations communicated to customers in product documentation.
regulatory.gapAction: Register as a WEEE producer with a UK-approved compliance scheme; include WEEE take-back information in the product manual and customer contract.

regulatory.name: Restriction of the Use of Certain Hazardous Substances in Electrical and Electronic Equipment Regulations 2012 (SI 2012/3032, as amended)
regulatory.summary: UK statutory instrument restricting the use of hazardous substances (lead, mercury, cadmium, hexavalent chromium, PBBs, PBDEs, DEHP, BBP, DBP, DIBP) in electrical and electronic equipment.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — Electronic sub-assemblies within the BESS (BMS boards, SCADA gateway, PCS control electronics, auxiliary LV distribution) must comply with RoHS substance restrictions; LFP cells are exempt as batteries under Schedule 2 but the electronic assemblies are not.
regulatory.designImpact: BMS, SCADA, and control electronics must be sourced from RoHS-compliant suppliers; technical documentation must include RoHS declarations for all in-scope sub-assemblies; any exemptions claimed must be documented.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: RoHS declarations of conformity from sub-assembly suppliers (BMS, SCADA, PCS control boards); include in UKCA technical file.
regulatory.gapAction: Request RoHS declarations of conformity from all electronic sub-assembly suppliers during procurement; compile declarations into the UKCA technical file.

regulatory.name: Commercial Property Insurer — BESS-specific underwriting requirements (market practice, 2023–2024)
regulatory.summary: UK commercial property and liability insurers apply specific underwriting requirements to BESS installations, typically referencing NFCC guidance, UL 9540A test data, and fire suppression standards.
