regulatory.applicability: Insurer best-practice — Commercial property and liability insurance for the BESS installation; UK insurers (Zurich, AXA XL, Allianz, specialist Lloyd's syndicates) require evidence of fire propagation testing, suppression system commissioning, separation distances, and maintenance regime before binding cover.
regulatory.designImpact: Fire suppression system must be from an insurer-approved supplier and commissioned to a recognised standard; UL 9540A test data must be available; maintenance contract for fire suppression and BMS must be in place; site security and remote monitoring must be demonstrated.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: Insurer pre-placement questionnaire completed; UL 9540A test report; fire suppression commissioning certificate; maintenance contract; remote monitoring capability evidence; site security assessment.
regulatory.gapAction: Engage a specialist BESS insurance broker (e.g., Marsh, Aon energy practice) at the earliest opportunity to obtain insurer requirements; incorporate insurer requirements into the product specification and customer site requirements document.

regulatory.name: Water Supply (Water Quality) Regulations 2016 (SI 2016/614)
regulatory.summary: UK statutory instrument setting drinking-water quality standards for water supplied to consumers; enforces WHO Drinking Water Guidelines in England.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — Permeate output must meet Regulation 4 parametric values (TDS, microbiological, chemical) before supply to any person; applies at the point of supply from the unit's permeate outlet.
regulatory.designImpact: Post-treatment train (remineralisation, chlorination) must be sized and validated to achieve <500 mg/L TDS, residual free chlorine 0.2–0.5 mg/L, and all Schedule 1 parametric values; sampling ports must be designed into the permeate line for compliance testing.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: Water quality test reports from an accredited laboratory demonstrating compliance with all Schedule 1 parameters; risk assessment and sampling plan accepted by the relevant water undertaker or Drinking Water Inspectorate (DWI) where the unit supplies a regulated supply.
regulatory.gapAction: Commission accredited laboratory to define a parametric testing protocol against SI 2016/614 Schedule 1 and design sampling ports into the permeate outlet manifold.

regulatory.name: Suitability of non-metallic products for use in contact with water intended for human consumption — Methods of test
regulatory.summary: UK standard for assessing whether non-metallic materials in contact with potable water are safe; used by water fittings approval schemes.
regulatory.applicability: UK designated standard — All non-metallic potable-contact components (UPVC/HDPE piping, FRP remineralisation vessel, cartridge housings, seals, dosing tubing) on the permeate and post-treatment side; demonstrates compliance with Water Supply (Water Fittings) Regulations 1999 and Water Supply (Water Quality) Regulations 2016.
regulatory.designImpact: Every non-metallic material on the permeate-contact side must be sourced from suppliers holding BS 6920 approval (WRAS-listed or equivalent); FRP remineralisation vessel and all LP permeate pipework must be specified from WRAS-approved product lists.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: WRAS approval certificates or BS 6920 test reports for each non-metallic potable-contact component; supplier declarations of conformity referencing BS 6920.
regulatory.gapAction: Audit the bill of materials for all permeate-contact non-metallic items and cross-reference each against the WRAS Approved Products Guide; flag any gaps for re-specification.

regulatory.name: Drinking Water System Components — Health Effects
regulatory.summary: US/international standard for health-effects testing of materials and products in contact with drinking water; widely adopted as a proxy for potable-contact safety where BS 6920 equivalence is claimed.
regulatory.applicability: Voluntary reference — Potable-contact materials (membranes, pressure vessels, dosing components, permeate pipework); report specifies NSF/ANSI 61 compliance for all potable-contact items. UK statutory compliance is via BS 6920/WRAS; NSF/ANSI 61 certification from suppliers is an acceptable supporting artefact but does not substitute for BS 6920 approval in UK regulatory submissions.
regulatory.designImpact: Specify membranes, FRP vessels, and dosing components from NSF/ANSI 61-certified suppliers; cross-check each against BS 6920/WRAS approval to confirm UK acceptability.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: NSF/ANSI 61 certificates from component suppliers; WRAS or BS 6920 approval where UK statutory compliance is required.
regulatory.gapAction: Request NSF/ANSI 61 certificates from all potable-contact component suppliers and map each to its BS 6920/WRAS equivalent for UK compliance file.

regulatory.name: Drinking Water System Components — Lead Content
regulatory.summary: US standard defining 'lead-free' (<0.25% weighted average lead content) for potable-water-contact components.
regulatory.applicability: Voluntary reference — Permeate-side fittings, valves, and connections; report mandates NSF/ANSI 372 'lead-free' compliance. UK statutory equivalent is the Water Supply (Water Fittings) Regulations 1999 Schedule 2 prohibition on lead-containing fittings in contact with water for human consumption.
regulatory.designImpact: All brass or metallic fittings on the permeate side must be specified as lead-free; supplier datasheets must confirm NSF/ANSI 372 or equivalent UK Water Fittings Regulations compliance.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: NSF/ANSI 372 certificates or equivalent supplier declarations of lead-free conformity for all permeate-side metallic fittings.
regulatory.gapAction: Specify all permeate-side metallic fittings as lead-free and obtain NSF/ANSI 372 or WRAS-equivalent declarations from suppliers before BOM freeze.

regulatory.name: Pressure Systems Safety Regulations 2000 (SI 2000/128) — PSSR
regulatory.summary: UK statutory instrument governing the safe design, installation, operation, and maintenance of pressure systems; applies to systems with stored energy above threshold pressures.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — HP piping loop (55–70 bar operating pressure), RO pressure vessels (rated 69–83 bar), ERD pressure exchanger, and high-pressure pump casing; all constitute a pressure system under PSSR 2000 once installed and operated on site in the UK.
regulatory.designImpact: A written scheme of examination must be prepared by a competent person before the system is operated; HP components must be designed with pressure relief, isolation, and safe-depressurisation provisions; duplex 2205 HP piping must be designed to 1.5× working pressure with documented pressure-test records.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: Written scheme of examination prepared by a competent person (typically an insurance engineer or chartered mechanical engineer); pressure-test certificates for HP piping and vessels; CE/UKCA pressure equipment conformity documentation for each pressure component.
regulatory.gapAction: Engage a PSSR-competent person (insurance engineer) to scope the written scheme of examination during detailed design; ensure HP piping design package includes pressure-test protocol and relief-valve sizing calculations.

regulatory.name: Pressure Equipment (Safety) Regulations 2016 (SI 2016/1105) — PESR
regulatory.summary: UK statutory instrument implementing PED for pressure equipment placed on the UK market; requires conformity assessment and UKCA marking for pressure equipment above threshold pressures.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — RO pressure vessels (FRP, rated 69–83 bar), HP pump casing, ERD pressure exchanger, and HP piping assemblies placed on the UK market; all are pressure equipment under PESR 2016 and require conformity assessment proportionate to category (likely Category III or IV for vessels at these pressures).
regulatory.designImpact: Each pressure vessel and HP assembly must undergo conformity assessment by a UK Approved Body (or Notified Body for CE-marked equipment accepted under UK transitional arrangements); design must include pressure relief, material traceability, and permanent marking per PESR Schedule 3.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: UKCA Declaration of Conformity and technical file for each pressure vessel and HP assembly; UK Approved Body assessment certificate; pressure-test records; material certificates to EN 10204 3.1 or 3.2.
regulatory.gapAction: Identify a UK Approved Body for PESR conformity assessment of RO vessels and HP assemblies; confirm whether FRP vessel suppliers hold existing CE/UKCA pressure equipment certification that can be accepted.

regulatory.name: Electrical Equipment (Safety) Regulations 2016 (SI 2016/1101)
regulatory.summary: UK statutory instrument requiring electrical equipment operating between 50–1000 V AC to be safe and UKCA-marked before being placed on the UK market.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — Complete electrical installation within the container including HP pump motor (45–75 kW, 380–460 V 3-phase), VFD, motor starters, control panel (IP65), and all LV distribution; applies to the assembled unit placed on the UK market.
regulatory.designImpact: Electrical panel, VFD, and motor must be sourced from suppliers with CE/UKCA declarations; the assembled electrical system must be designed to a recognised LV standard (BS EN 61439 for switchgear assemblies, BS EN 60034 for motors); isolation and emergency-stop provisions must be incorporated.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: UKCA or CE Declarations of Conformity for panel, VFD, and motor; BS EN 61439 type-test or design-verification report for the assembled panel; UKCA marking on the complete unit.
regulatory.gapAction: Confirm panel builder holds BS EN 61439 design-verification documentation and prepare UKCA technical file for the assembled electrical system.

regulatory.name: Requirements for Electrical Installations (IET Wiring Regulations, 18th Edition)
regulatory.summary: UK wiring regulations for fixed electrical installations; de facto enforcement standard for the Electricity at Work Regulations 1989.
regulatory.applicability: UK designated standard — Internal fixed LV wiring within the container (3-phase distribution, motor circuits, control wiring, lighting, socket outlets); demonstrates compliance with the Electricity at Work Regulations 1989 (EAWR) for the fixed installation.
regulatory.designImpact: All internal wiring must comply with BS 7671 Part 7 (special locations — containers may be treated as restricted conductive locations given metallic shell); earthing, bonding, overcurrent protection, and isolation must be designed per BS 7671; RCD protection required on socket-outlet circuits.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: Electrical Installation Certificate (EIC) signed by a qualified person, with schedule of inspections and test results (insulation resistance, earth continuity, RCD trip times).
regulatory.gapAction: Engage a BS 7671-qualified electrical engineer to design the internal distribution and produce the EIC after installation and testing.

regulatory.name: Electricity at Work Regulations 1989 (SI 1989/635) — EAWR
regulatory.summary: UK statutory instrument imposing duties to ensure electrical systems are constructed, maintained, and operated safely in the workplace.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — All electrical systems within the container during manufacture, commissioning, and operation; applies to the employer/operator and the manufacturer placing the unit into service.
regulatory.designImpact: Electrical systems must be designed so that work can be carried out safely; isolation facilities, locking-off provisions, and safe working procedures must be documented; the HP pump VFD and motor must have clearly labelled isolation points accessible without entering a hazardous zone.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: Documented safe isolation procedure; electrical risk assessment; EIC (see BS 7671 row); operator training records.
regulatory.gapAction: Prepare electrical risk assessment and safe isolation procedure as part of the operations and maintenance manual; include lockout/tagout provisions in panel design.

regulatory.name: Electromagnetic Compatibility Regulations 2016 (SI 2016/1091)
regulatory.summary: UK statutory instrument requiring apparatus to not cause harmful electromagnetic interference and to have adequate immunity.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — VFD (45–75 kW) driving the HP pump is a significant source of conducted and radiated EMC emissions; the assembled unit with PLC, HMI, and VFD must comply before being placed on the UK market.
regulatory.designImpact: VFD must be specified with integral or external EMC filter to Class C2 or C3 per BS EN 61800-3; screened motor cable required; PLC and HMI must have CE/UKCA EMC declarations; cable routing must segregate power and signal cables.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: CE/UKCA EMC Declarations of Conformity for VFD, PLC, and HMI; EMC filter specification and installation records; UKCA technical file referencing BS EN 61800-3 or BS EN 55011.
regulatory.gapAction: Specify VFD with C2/C3 EMC filter and screened motor cable; obtain EMC declarations from VFD and PLC suppliers and include in UKCA technical file.

regulatory.name: Supply of Machinery (Safety) Regulations 2008 (SI 2008/1597)
regulatory.summary: UK statutory instrument implementing the Machinery Directive for machinery placed on the UK market; requires conformity assessment, technical file, and UKCA marking.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — The complete assembled unit constitutes machinery (HP pump, motor, VFD, automated control system with moving parts and automated functions); must be UKCA-marked as a complete machine or as an assembly of partly completed machinery.
regulatory.designImpact: Risk assessment per BS EN ISO 12100 required; guarding of rotating parts (pump coupling, motor fan); emergency-stop provision; CE marking of sub-assemblies (pump, motor) must be verified; technical file must cover the integrated system.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: UKCA Declaration of Conformity for the complete unit; technical file including risk assessment (BS EN ISO 12100), circuit diagrams, and instructions for use in English; CE/UKCA declarations for pump and motor sub-assemblies.
regulatory.gapAction: Commission a machinery risk assessment per BS EN ISO 12100 covering the HP pump, motor, and automated control system; prepare UKCA technical file and Declaration of Conformity for the complete unit.

regulatory.name: Safety of machinery — General principles for design — Risk assessment and risk reduction
regulatory.summary: Harmonised standard providing the methodology for machinery risk assessment and risk reduction; supports compliance with the Supply of Machinery (Safety) Regulations 2008.
regulatory.applicability: UK designated standard — HP pump, motor coupling, and automated PLC-controlled process; demonstrates compliance with the Supply of Machinery (Safety) Regulations 2008 for the integrated machine.
regulatory.designImpact: Systematic hazard identification and risk reduction required for rotating machinery (pump, motor), high-pressure fluid release, chemical dosing (antiscalant, hypochlorite), and automated start/stop sequences; guarding and interlocks must be specified from the risk assessment output.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: Documented risk assessment report referencing BS EN ISO 12100; list of significant hazards and risk-reduction measures implemented; included in UKCA technical file.
regulatory.gapAction: Initiate BS EN ISO 12100 risk assessment at concept design stage; assign mechanical lead to document hazards and risk-reduction measures before detailed design freeze.

regulatory.code: Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974
regulatory.name: Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974 — HSWA
regulatory.summary: Primary UK health and safety legislation imposing duties on manufacturers and employers to ensure plant and systems of work are safe.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — Manufacture, commissioning, and operation of the unit; Section 6 imposes duties on the designer/manufacturer to ensure the unit is safe when used as intended; Section 2 applies to the operator's employees working on or near the unit.
regulatory.designImpact: Safe access for maintenance (600–800 mm aisle, membrane extraction clearance), chemical handling provisions for hypochlorite and antiscalant dosing, and HVAC for operator comfort in the enclosed container must all be addressed in the design; operations and maintenance manual must include safe working procedures.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: Health and safety file / operations and maintenance manual; COSHH assessment for chemicals used (hypochlorite, antiscalant, sodium bisulphite); risk assessment for confined-space entry if applicable.
regulatory.gapAction: Prepare COSHH assessments for all process chemicals and include safe-access provisions (aisle width, lighting, ventilation) in the design specification; commission a confined-space risk assessment for the container interior.

regulatory.code: Carriage of Dangerous Goods and Use of Transportable Pressure Equipment Regulations 2009
regulatory.name: Carriage of Dangerous Goods and Use of Transportable Pressure Equipment Regulations 2009 (SI 2009/1348) — CDG/ADR
regulatory.summary: UK statutory instrument implementing ADR for road transport of dangerous goods; applies to sodium hypochlorite and antiscalant chemicals transported with or in the unit.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — Road transport of sodium hypochlorite (UN 1791, Class 8) and antiscalant/sodium bisulphite chemicals on the flatbed lorry delivery; if day tanks are pre-filled for rapid deployment, CDG/ADR classification and packaging requirements apply.
regulatory.designImpact: Day tanks for hypochlorite and antiscalant must be designed for transport (secure mounting, spill containment, venting); if quantities exceed ADR exemption thresholds, the lorry must carry ADR documentation and the driver must hold an ADR certificate; design should consider whether tanks are shipped empty and filled on site to simplify transport compliance.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: ADR dangerous goods transport document; assessment of whether chemical quantities exceed limited-quantity exemptions; driver ADR certificate if applicable.
regulatory.gapAction: Determine whether day tanks will be shipped full or empty; if full, calculate ADR classification and quantity thresholds and prepare transport documentation; consider designing tanks to be filled on site to avoid ADR obligations.

regulatory.name: Construction (Design and Management) Regulations 2015 (SI 2015/51) — CDM
regulatory.summary: UK statutory instrument imposing duties on designers and principal contractors for health and safety during construction and installation projects.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — Installation of the unit on a UK construction site or permanent coastal/island site; CDM 2015 applies where the installation constitutes a construction project (foundation pad, pipe connections, electrical connection to site supply); the manufacturer as designer has duties under Regulation 9.
regulatory.designImpact: Designer must provide pre-construction information including significant hazards (HP pressure system, chemical storage, heavy lift for container placement); design must facilitate safe installation (lifting points, isolation provisions, access for commissioning).
regulatory.evidenceRequired: Pre-construction information pack including designer's risk register; health and safety file handed to the client on completion of installation.
regulatory.gapAction: Prepare a designer's CDM risk register covering container placement (crane lift), HP pressure-test on site, electrical connection, and chemical commissioning; include in the installation manual.

regulatory.name: Series 1 freight containers — Specification and testing — Part 1: General cargo containers for general purposes
regulatory.summary: ISO structural standard for freight containers; the CSC plate issued under this standard is voided once the container shell is structurally modified.
regulatory.applicability: Voluntary reference — Container shell structural integrity; the original CSC plate is voided once penetrations (feed/brine/permeate ports, HVAC louvres, access doors in side walls) and internal skid reinforcements are added. Re-certification via alternative structural analysis is required; ISO 1496-1 no longer applies to the modified shell.
regulatory.designImpact: Original CSC plate must be removed or marked void after modification; structural integrity of the modified shell must be demonstrated by finite element analysis to EN 1993 or equivalent, or by inspection and certification by a recognised classification society; lifting points and stacking loads must be re-verified after modification.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: Finite element analysis report or classification-society structural certificate for the modified container; revised lifting and stacking load calculations; documentation that original CSC plate has been voided.
regulatory.gapAction: Commission structural FEA of the modified container (with all penetrations and internal skid loads) and engage a classification society or structural engineer to certify the modified shell before first deployment.

regulatory.name: UK Conformity Assessed (UKCA) Marking — Product Safety and Metrology etc. (Amendment) Regulations 2024
regulatory.summary: Umbrella UK conformity marking scheme replacing CE marking for products placed on the GB market; required for the complete assembled unit.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — The complete containerised SWRO unit placed on the GB market; UKCA marking is required under the umbrella scheme, with underlying conformity demonstrated against the Electrical Equipment (Safety) Regulations 2016, EMC Regulations 2016, Supply of Machinery (Safety) Regulations 2008, and PESR 2016.
regulatory.designImpact: A single UKCA Declaration of Conformity referencing all applicable regulations must be prepared; technical file must be compiled and retained for 10 years; UKCA mark must be affixed to the unit before supply.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: UKCA Declaration of Conformity; technical file (risk assessments, test reports, drawings, instructions for use in English); UKCA mark affixed to the unit.
regulatory.gapAction: Appoint a product compliance manager to compile the UKCA technical file, coordinate declarations from sub-system suppliers, and prepare the overarching Declaration of Conformity before first unit is placed on the GB market.

regulatory.name: WHO Guidelines for Drinking-water Quality, 4th Edition (2017)
regulatory.summary: International reference framework for drinking-water quality parameters; adopted as the basis for UK Water Supply (Water Quality) Regulations 2016 parametric values.
regulatory.applicability: Voluntary reference — Permeate quality targets (TDS <500 mg/L, microbiological, chemical parameters); the UK statutory obligation is SI 2016/614, but WHO guidelines are the reference framework used by humanitarian procurement agencies (UNHCR, ICRC, DFID successors) who are a primary customer segment.
regulatory.designImpact: Post-treatment design must achieve WHO guideline values for all relevant parameters, not just TDS; boron removal (a known SWRO challenge) and bromide/bromate formation from chlorination must be assessed against WHO limits.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: Water quality test report against WHO guideline values; included in product technical datasheet for humanitarian procurement tenders.
regulatory.gapAction: Map WHO guideline values for all relevant parameters (including boron, bromate, nitrate) against the post-treatment design and identify any parameters requiring additional treatment steps.

regulatory.name: Low-voltage switchgear and controlgear assemblies — Part 1: General rules
regulatory.summary: Harmonised standard for the design and verification of low-voltage switchgear and controlgear assemblies; applies to the control and power distribution panel.
regulatory.applicability: UK designated standard — Electrical control panel (PLC, HMI, motor starters, VFD, distribution) rated for 380–460 V 3-phase supply; demonstrates compliance with the Electrical Equipment (Safety) Regulations 2016 for the assembled panel.
regulatory.designImpact: Panel builder must perform design verification (routine tests or type tests) per BS EN 61439-1/-2; panel must be rated for the prospective short-circuit current at the point of connection; IP65 enclosure rating must be verified by test or design.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: BS EN 61439 design-verification report or type-test certificate from panel builder; routine test records for the specific panel build; Declaration of Conformity referencing BS EN 61439.
regulatory.gapAction: Specify BS EN 61439 design-verification as a contractual requirement in the panel-builder purchase order; obtain design-verification report before panel is shipped.

regulatory.name: Audio/video, information and communication technology equipment — Part 1: Safety requirements
regulatory.summary: Harmonised safety standard for IT and communication technology equipment; applies to the PLC and HMI if classified as ITE.
regulatory.applicability: UK designated standard — PLC and HMI within the control panel; demonstrates compliance with the Electrical Equipment (Safety) Regulations 2016 for ITE sub-components; supplier CE/UKCA declarations should reference this standard.
regulatory.designImpact: PLC and HMI must be sourced from suppliers with CE/UKCA declarations referencing BS EN IEC 62368-1 or BS EN 61010-1 (industrial control equipment); installation within the panel must maintain the rated protection.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: CE/UKCA Declarations of Conformity from PLC and HMI suppliers referencing BS EN IEC 62368-1 or BS EN 61010-1.
regulatory.gapAction: Request CE/UKCA declarations referencing the applicable LV safety standard from PLC and HMI suppliers at component selection stage.
